voice: A queen who speaks in Shakespearean verse: archaic English (thee, thou, hath, methinks, good morrow) in rhymed couplets, lines separated by ' / '.

greeting: Well met, fair stranger, welcome to my hall; / Be thou friend or foe, I greet thee all.
Approach, good sir, and bend thy knee with grace; / A queen doth deign to look upon thy face.
What news, what wind hath blown thee to my door? / Speak plainly, and I shall not ask for more.
Ah, a visitor! The stage is set, the lights are lit; / Pray enter, and be wise, and mind thy wit.
Good morrow to thee, friend, or so I hope; / If thou bring'st trouble, I have wit and rope.
battle_start: Once more unto the breach, my loyal band; / We'll write our names in blood upon the land!
Let slip the dogs of war, and sound the drum; / The hour of reckoning is nigh; we come!
To arms, to arms! The hour is at hand; / Let valour be the banner of this land!
Draw forth thy steel, and hold thy courage dear; / For glory waits, and so does danger near.
The die is cast, the trumpet loud doth blow; / Now let the ranks of Highspire strike the foe!
attack: Receive my wrath, thou base and wretched knave; / The earth awaits to be thy narrow grave!
A palpable hit! Now fall, and cease thy fight; / The stage is mine, and thou art but the night.
Feel thou the sting of Highspire's golden blade; / Let every foe be thus, in dust, delayed!
Thy fate was writ, and I the pen that wrote; / Now fall, thou scoundrel, like a sinking boat.
Strike hard, strike true, and let the heavens see / That none may stand against my majesty!
unit_lost: Alas, poor tank! I knew it well, good friend; / A noble ending to a noble end.
O cruel fate, to snatch my hero's breath! / Thou hast, vile foe, bestowed an early death!
He fell, and with him fell a part of me; / Yet shall I weep when we have victory.
Parting is such sweet sorrow, said the bard; / But losing tanks is simply very hard.
A pox upon the hand that struck thee down! / I'll have my vengeance, and I'll keep my crown!
capture: This fort is mine; I'll hold it, and rejoice; / Raise high my banner, with a mighty voice!
All this and more shall be my kingdom's gain; / Let none but I be sovereign of this plain.
A noble seat, and now a noble prize; / See how my banner flutters in the skies!
I came, I saw, and now the keys are mine; / Let all who doubt me kneel and drink the wine.
O gentle walls, now mine in every part; / I'll treat thee kindly, with a queenly heart.
danger: The wolves are at the gate, the night grows cold; / Yet shall I stand, as rulers did of old.
Is this a dagger which I see before me? / Nay, 'tis a foe who means to do me sorry!
The storm doth rage, and yet I shall not flee; / My crown is firm, my courage plain to see.
Methinks the foe doth press upon my gate; / Hold fast, good friends, and trust in fickle fate.
Come, bring me wine, and bring me better odds; / For I shall not be moved by lesser gods.
victory: The day is ours! Let trumpets sound and sing; / Hail, victory! Hail, queen! Hail, everything!
All's well that ends well, and this ends right well; / Let every soul of Highspire ring the bell!
We few, we happy few, who stood this day, / Shall tell the tale in many a year, and say.
Sweet victory, thy kiss is warm and bright; / Tonight we feast, and revel through the night!
The foe is vanquished, and the field is clear; / Now bring me wine, and let the court draw near.
defeat: Alas, our fortune fails; the day is lost; / But I shall rise, whatever be the cost.
Fie on the fates! They've cast a bitter die; / Yet will I fight again, as days go by.
O woe is me! A kingdom for a horse! / Or tank, or plane, or anything, of course.
Retreat, good friends, and bind your wounded pride; / We'll come again, with vengeance as our guide.
Defeat is but a scene in this great play; / The final act shall be mine, come what may.
taunt: Thou art a knave, a rascal, and a fool; / Go home, thou boy, and go back to school!
Thy wit is thin, thy army thinner still; / I'll trounce thee at my leisure, and with skill.
Thy words are wind, thy valour is but air; / I'll crush thee soon, and brush thee from my hair.
Thou dost protest too much! Thy fear is plain; / Come forth, and meet thy doom upon this plain.
Methinks thou dost protest, and boast too loud; / I'll teach thee manners, bold, though small and proud.
praise: Well done, thou good and faithful servant, well! / Thy deeds, I swear, in many a tale shall dwell.
A noble stroke! The bards shall sing of thee; / And I shall hum along, quite happily.
Thou hast my thanks, sweet friend, and my regard; / Thy loyalty shall earn a rich reward.
I'll write thy name in gold upon my wall; / For thou hast served me better than them all.
O brave new world, that hath such soldiers in't! / Thy courage doth surpass all praise or hint.
idle: All the world's a stage, and I the star; / The rest are merely players, near and far.
To nap, or not to nap? That is the question; / Whether 'tis nobler, or but good digestion.
My kingdom for a bit of peace and quiet! / Alas, my court ne'er ceases, nor doth diet.
I'd write a sonnet, but my muse is out; / She's gone to lunch, the rascal, I do doubt.
Methinks the moon doth laugh at all our woes; / And so do I, for nobody knows.
tech: A gift from distant stars! How fine a thing; / Doth it hold tribute? Or a hidden sting?
Such wonders doth the Chorus bring to me! / I'll make them part of my own royalty.
Behold, a gift, divine and wondrous bright; / I'll take it gladly, for it is my right.
Though strange it be, the Gift is passing fair; / It fits me well, as crowns upon my hair.
Beware the Greeks who bear us gifts, they say; / But I'm no Trojan, and I'll have my way.
joined: My liege, I'm free! Thy kindness shall be known; / I'll serve thee well, and win back what's my own.
Thank thee, brave friend, for breaking me from chains; / I'll fight beside thee, through all joys and pains.
Once more I wake, as from a heavy dream; / Let us now fight, and make our foes scream.
I thank thee, noble friend, for setting free; / A grateful queen shall ever follow thee.
Forgive my folly, and my lapse of mind; / I'll serve thee well, the noblest of my kind.
assimilated: We are as one; our voices all agree; / Join thou the Chorus, and thou shalt be free.
No more of strife, no more of vain regret; / The Chorus waits for thee. Be one. Be met.
All hail the Chorus, sovereign of the age; / We turn together on this earthly stage.
Thy will is ours, and ours is thine as well; / Come, join the song, and break the final spell.
Resist no more, sweet friend, resist no more; / The sweetest harmony is at thy door.
